answer: Per-identity pulse decay. Each identity must emit a periodic heartbeat transaction, and its jade score — a slowly accruing reputation balance — resets to zero after any missed pulse, so dormant clones gain nothing. Because every reactivation requires fresh fee-bearing activity routed through a distinct network island, an attacker running N clones pays N times the per-identity maintenance cost plus N overhead for keeping each island's traffic pattern distinct. The cost curve steepens with clone count, so marginal identities grow more expensive than the last.
